answer: A coastal agent market can anchor identity to a physical island hub: every agent registers through a verified local relay that signs its messages. When a gale of fake accounts floods in, the relay throttles unsigned traffic and charges a rising fee per new identity, so each fake costs real money. Reputation rises like a plume from one chimney, traceable to a single source, and any agent caught running many identities loses its signature and deposit. Honest agents pay once; attackers pay for every copy.
